records.quote: Rationale for microgravity remains the same for all the droplet combustion experiments conducted onboard the ISS.
records.derivation: Rationale statement (Final Report section 3b); it implies, but does not state, that the CFI tests were burned in microgravity. 'onboard the ISS' is a platform, not a gravity statement.

records.quote: Flame combustion of liquid hydrocarbon fuels such as n-dodecane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures, and faresane in microgravity can provide insights into low-temperature chemical kinetics, revealing critical parameters like droplet extinction diameters and flame dynamics that are not observable on Earth.
records.derivation: Hypothesis field: names microgravity as the intended condition, not as a reported condition of the tests.

records.quote: The overall goal of the proposed experiments is to improve our understanding of low temperature chemistry by studying the cool flame burning and, most importantly, cool flame extinction of droplet burning with spherical symmetry in a long-duration microgravity environment.
records.derivation: Pre-flight objective (SRD dated November 7, 2014, 'proposed experiments'); not a statement about the tests as run.

records.quote: Flame combustion of liquid hydrocarbon fuels such as n-dodecane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures, and faresane in microgravity can provide insights into low-temperature chemical kinetics, revealing critical parameters like droplet extinction diameters and flame dynamics that are not observable on Earth.
Subsequently, a droplet of desired size is dispensed between the hypodermic needles and freely deployed, and ignited.
records.derivation: A fuel droplet dispensed between hypodermic needles is a liquid; the sentence (post-flight procedure) does not name the phase.

records.quote: CFI experiments were conducted onboard the ISS from January 2017 through September 2017.
The Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) contains the Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) which facilitates the controlled combustion of fuel droplets.
records.note: SHARED_LINEAGE: same CIR/MDCA hardware as FLEX and FLEX-2 (Final Report page 6: 'The experimental hardware is same as that of the FLEX experiments with few minor modifications in the data acquisition systems.').

records.quote: The Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) contains the Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) which facilitates the controlled combustion of fuel droplets.
records.note: SHARED_LINEAGE: same CIR/MDCA hardware as FLEX and FLEX-2 (Final Report page 6: 'The experimental hardware is same as that of the FLEX experiments with few minor modifications in the data acquisition systems.').

records.quote: The proposed CFI experiments involve igniting and observing the burning behavior of relatively large droplets. The experiments seek to observe [...] cool flame extinction of primarily free-floated fuel droplets in q quiescent ambient envrionment.
records.derivation: Pre-flight plan (SRD dated November 7, 2014, section 6.1, 'proposed CFI experiments'); the Final Report (2020) does not restate the flow configuration. 'q quiescent' and 'envrionment' are typos in the source, kept verbatim.

records.quote: Ambient Quiescience: gases shall be well-mixed and quiescent prior to ignition.
records.derivation: Pre-flight requirement ('shall'), stated for the gas prior to ignition; the Final Report does not restate it.

records.quote: The MDCA is capable of deploying both free and fiber-supported droplets in a quiescent microgravity environment.
records.derivation: Sentence is in the SRD's FLEX hardware section (2.3.1) and describes MDCA capability; it applies to CFI only through the shared hardware (Final Report page 6: 'The experimental hardware is same as that of the FLEX experiments').
records.note: SHARED_LINEAGE: MDCA hardware shared with FLEX and FLEX-2.

records.quote: Ambient temperature: initial chamber gas temperature shall be 18 − 27 C.
records.derivation: Pre-flight requirement band ('shall be', SRD dated November 7, 2014) for the initial chamber gas temperature; no as-run chamber temperature is reported in the Final Report or the record text. Unit written as 'C' without a degree sign. Same band appears in Table 1, page 35 ('initial gas temperature at 18 - 27 C').

records.quote: The initial combustion chamber temperature will be maintained around 250 C and the relative humidity maintained at less than 10%.
records.derivation: PDF text layer reads '250 C', but the rendered page shows '25' followed by a superscript '0' used as a degree sign, i.e. about 25 degrees C, consistent with R13 (18 − 27 C). Do NOT use 250 as a value. Also a pre-flight plan ('will be maintained'), approximate ('around').

not_found.looked_in: No sentence stating that the CFI tests themselves were burned in microgravity (only rationale, hypothesis and pre-flight objective sentences, proposed as ambiguous R1-R3); no normal-gravity (1-g) comparison tests reported (SRD page 36 lists two fuels 'for ground-based testing only', with no reported results). Looked in: record text (all sections), SRD pages 1-54, Final Report pages 1-13.

No as-run (measured) chamber temperature for the CFI tests; only SRD pre-flight requirements (R13, R14). Final Report page 3 values '700 to 900 K' and 'higher than 1200 K' are flame temperatures from FLEX, not ambient. Looked in: record text, SRD pages 1-54, Final Report pages 1-13.
Record text and Final Report pages 1-13 do not state the flow configuration (no 'quiescent', no forced flow mentioned); only SRD pre-flight statements and MDCA hardware description (R10-R12).

lineage: Same hardware as FLEX and FLEX-2 (MDCA in the CIR): Final Report page 6, 'The experimental hardware is same as that of the FLEX experiments with few minor modifications in the data acquisition systems.' CFI tests are archived under FLEX test numbers (Final Report page 7: 'Pure n-dodecane data: FLEX-1206 to FLEX-1284'). Caution: SRD sections 2.3-2.5 (pages 12-29, Figures 2-10) report FLEX/FLEX-2/FLEX-ICE-GA heptane, octane and decane tests, not CFI tests; their conditions must not be attributed to PSI-39.
